bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and accepts POST requests containing an attacker-controlled exec string. Authentication is fail-open: WebhookServer.authenticate returns true whenever the configured token is empty, a state the configuration comments explicitly describe as 'empty = no auth'. The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. Thus an attacker who supplies a nonempty, reconstructable session_key (and a project when multiple projects are configured) can execute an arbitrary shell program as the cc-connect process without a credential. The shell interpretation of exec is an intentional feature; the security failure is exposing that full shell capability across a network endpoint while treating an omitted token as authorization.
flaw_origin: The complete vulnerable mechanism originated in the single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38: it created core/webhook.go, added the network listener and /hook handler, defined the JSON exec field, made an empty token authenticate successfully, passed exec to sh -c, wired the server into main, and documented an empty token as disabling authentication. This is the smallest repository-visible BIC, not the later shell-helper refactor.
ai_marker: BIC commit object has human author and committer 'chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn>' and contains the exact message lines 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The latter is an explicit AI co-authorship trailer on the BIC itself.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1488 identifies core/webhook.go's empty-token authentication bypass, exec dispatch, all-interface listener, and shell sink; maintainer @chenhg5 replied on 2026-07-03 that the report was confirmed valid and described the same two-part chain. Source review adds an important reachability qualification: handleHook requires a nonempty session_key, resolveEngine must succeed, and executeShell must reconstruct the named platform context. Consequently, the issue's displayed curl body, which omits session_key, would be rejected at the required-field check, but adding a valid/reconstructable session key reaches the confirmed unauthenticated shell path.

`git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go config/config.go config.example.toml cmd/cc-connect/main.go` shows one cohesive +503-line webhook feature. In core/webhook.go it creates WebhookRequest.Exec, starts http.Server at fmt.Sprintf(":%d", ws.port), routes POST /hook through authenticate, returns true for ws.token == "", dispatches req.Exec, and runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). config/config.go and config.example.toml state that an empty token means no authentication, while main.go starts the listener whenever webhook.enabled is true.

The BIC's newly added core/webhook_test.go makes the insecure policy explicit: TestWebhookServer_NoTokenRequired creates a server with an empty token and asserts authenticate succeeds. The same test file validates that exec is accepted as one of the two request action types, corroborating that no-token access and network-triggered exec were deliberately shipped together rather than accidentally joined by later history.

History searches `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""' -- core/webhook.go` and `git log --all -S 'req.Exec' -- core/webhook.go` each identify 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 as the first writer. The complete path log contains only the introducer, a later broad error-handling commit b9af7ea7ba641eb9278d45c9a19f361692acef44, and shell-configuration refactor 6feaf90f2f8cccec2203169b4d0edc3edd538837. The latter only replaces direct sh -c construction with shellExecCommand while continuing to pass req.Exec, so it preserves rather than introduces the vulnerable trust boundary.

Immediate-parent verification is direct: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 -- core/webhook.go` returns no path, and `git diff-tree --name-status 805045501b12fd3cf3834d19b0b882b32803e8c2 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go` reports `A core/webhook.go`. Therefore the parent tree lacks the endpoint, empty-token bypass, request exec field, and webhook shell sink. The BIC is a one-parent public-DAG feature commit; no smaller reachable member commits exist to decompose.

Release-boundary check: v1.2.2-beta.1 resolves to ecea1ef36d86bb70dd633fb342f655d108ea52cb (2026-03-12) and lacks core/webhook.go, while the 2026-03-14 BIC is contained by v1.2.2-beta.2, which resolves to 9223201696e3f91b2f9fb456bba7dcef0a76bcd3 (2026-03-16). `git tag --contains 6ae088a...` starts at v1.2.2-beta.2 and includes v1.4.1. Direct `git grep` confirms both `if ws.token == ""` and the req.Exec shell sink in v1.2.2-beta.2 and v1.4.1; v1.2.2-beta.1 has neither. This places the introduction before the affected upper-bound release named by the advisory.

No fix is present in the validated public history. `git log --all -- core/webhook.go` has no post-6feaf90 remediation, `git log --all -S 'if ws.token == ""'` has no removal, and direct tag-tree checks show the bypass plus req.Exec-to-shell path still present in stable v1.5.0 (17c61062c2f9ce9bcdd45a2082e491f9743a2770, 2026-08-16) and HEAD/v1.5.1-beta.1 (80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4, 2026-08-28). Issue #1488 was auto-closed for inactivity rather than by a patch. fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are therefore null; the advisory summary's 'up to 1.4.1' wording is not a demonstrated patched boundary and the source remains vulnerable in later tags.

Because this same object first writes every causal component, the explicit AI co-authorship is attached to the root-cause introduction, satisfying AI_ROOT_CAUSE without relying on issue/PR prose, branch names, or later commits.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a composed trust-boundary failure, not merely the existence of a shell API. With webhook.enabled true, the BIC binds the webhook listener to every interface; an omitted token causes authenticate to approve every caller; handleHook accepts a caller-provided exec action; and executeShell supplies that string as the shell program. A usable request also needs a session key whose platform context can be reconstructed, and possibly a project selector, but neither substitutes for authentication. The 6ae088a commit introduced all of these pieces at once and even added a test requiring empty-token authentication to pass. Its immediate parent has no core/webhook.go or equivalent webhook-exec route, so absence is tree-proven. Pickaxe history finds no earlier writer, while the only later sink change is a behavior-preserving helper refactor. Tag membership brackets introduction between v1.2.2-beta.1 and v1.2.2-beta.2 and confirms persistence through the advisory's v1.4.1 boundary. There is no remediation commit: both the latest stable tag and audited HEAD retain the bypass and shell dispatch, so null fix fields are justified and unpatched status is recorded. Finally, the smallest BIC's own commit object explicitly says `generated by llmgit` and credits Claude as co-author. Since that AI-marked object is the first writer of the flawed authentication-plus-exec design, the causal verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in every fetched ref of the validated clone through HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 and v1.5.1-beta.1; therefore no fix SHA or direct-fix SHA exists to audit. A future remediation commit and patched release boundary are the only outstanding lifecycle facts.
